'''CZ-1''' was a [[CZ-series secretary/business communications droid]] that was paired with [[CZ-3]], another [[droid]] of the same model. After a crash left him abandoned on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]], CZ-1 became separated from CZ-3 and ended up in a pile of scrap on board a [[Jawa]] [[sandcrawler]], where he encountered the [[R2-series astromech droid|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2]] in [[1 BBY]].

==Biography==
CZ-1 was the designation<ref name="Visual Dictionary" /> of a [[CZ-series secretary/business communications droid]] manufactured by [[Serv-O-Droid, Inc.]].<ref name="Build R2 9" /> He was twinned with fellow CZ unit [[CZ-3]] in service to members of the [[Stacchati]] [[species]].<ref name="Visual Dictionary" />

After a crash in the [[desert]]s of the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]], CZ-1 was abandoned and became separated from CZ-3. He then broke down and was captured by [[Jawa]] [[scavenger]]s.<ref name="Visual Dictionary" /> In [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Date">{{FilmDate|IV|1|CZ-1's appearance}}</ref> the [[secretary droid]]<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" /> was on board the [[sandcrawler]]<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> of the Jawa [[Chief]] [[Nebit]]'s [[Nebit's tribe|tribe]]<ref name="Force Collection">{{ForceCollection|Nebit|star=1}}</ref> when the [[R2-series astromech droid|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2]] was brought on board after being captured<ref name="ANH" /> in the [[Jundland Wastes]].<ref name="Complete Locations">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref>

As the [[Astromech droid|astromech]] rolled past CZ-1 while surveying his surroundings, the secretary [[droid]] swayed back and forth amidst a heap of scrap.<ref name="Novelization">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (paperback novel)|''Star Wars: A New Hope'' junior novelization]]</ref> R2-D2 was later sold when the sandcrawler stopped at the [[Lars homestead|Lars moisture farm]], after which [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[stormtrooper]]s [[Death|massacred]] Nebit's tribe and left its sandcrawler abandoned in the desert.<ref name="ANH" />

==Characteristics==
CZ-1 was modified from a standard CZ-series droid to more closely resemble the Stacchati he once served, with [[Color|black]] [[photoreceptor]]s made to look like Stacchati [[eye]]s. The droid's [[Limb|hands]] were [[human]]-style manipulators with five digits.<ref name="Visual Dictionary" /> By 1 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]],<ref name="Date" /> CZ-1 was ancient<ref name="Novelization" /> with [[locomotor]]s too broken and sand-encrusted for him to stand or move properly. Despite this, he remained optimistic and hoped to soon be repaired and sold. CZ-1 had white plating that was stained black or brown in many areas.<ref name="Visual Dictionary" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I seem to remember at the time it was one of the original concepts for Vader.|Brian Muir, on CZ-1's head|<ref name="Costumes">''[[Star Wars Costumes: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref>}}
CZ-1 first appeared in the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="ANH" /> In the current [[canon]], the droid first received identification in the [[2017]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'', which was written by [[Tricia Barr]], [[Adam Bray]] and [[Cole Horton]].<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" /> The droid's name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used in the [[1998]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]'', which was written by [[David West Reynolds (real person)|David West Reynolds]].<ref name="Complete Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

[[File:CZ_Head.png|thumb|right|200px|Muir felt CZ-1's pupils gave the droid a humorous effect.]]
Sculptor [[Brian Muir]] made the head for CZ-1, who was known as the "Tatooine [[protocol droid]]," based on an illustration by concept artist [[Ralph McQuarrie]], which Muir remembers being one of the original designs for the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]. Muir felt the paint job applied to the costume did not quite capture the essence he intended it to have, as the pupils on the white eyes gave it an unintentionally humorous effect. Muir's mentor, [[Arthur Healey]], sculpted CZ-1's chest, which also resembled an early sketch of Vader by concept artist [[John Mollo]].<ref name="Costumes" />

The droid's limbs were manufactured from [[Wikipedia:Aluminum|aluminum]] to be lightweight and durable, and were essentially the same as the [[3PO-series protocol droid|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO]]'s limbs but with slightly different detailing. The major difference when compared to C-3PO was that the trunks of the costume did not tuck inside the legs, but instead sat outside of them. The Tatooine protocol droid costume was used three times in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' films: twice in ''A New Hope'' for both CZ-1 and CZ-3, and once in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] for a droid in [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]]<ref name="Costumes" /> named [[CZ-4]].<ref name="Build R2 9" />
